title: Canada Post narrows Q3 loss to $451M as parcel and flyer business picks up

blocks.text: The third-quarter loss is an improvement of nearly 17 per cent, compared with the $541-million loss in the same period last year. The postal carrier has been struggling as fewer people send letter mail.
Postal carrier struggling as fewer people send letters in the mail
Canada Post says it lost hundreds of millions of dollars in its latest quarter — but still far less than a year earlier as its parcel and flyer business continues to recover.
The Crown corporation is reporting a before-tax loss of $451 million for the three months ended Sept. 30, an improvement of nearly 17 per cent from the $541-million loss in the same period last year.
The postal service attributed the better results to a cash surge from parcel shipments, as well as flyers and other direct marketing, while letter mail stayed flat.

items: Feds greenlight $673M to keep Canada Post afloat this year

blocks.text: Parcel revenue jumped by $140 million, or 31 per cent year-over-year, as 13 million more packages were shipped, while direct marketing revenue rose by $35 million, or 17 per cent, due to a volume increase of 291 million pieces.
Canada Post has been struggling with debt in recent years as fewer people are sending letter mail and parcel volumes fell. In 2025, it logged $1.57 billion in losses before tax — its worst on record.
Breaking down Canada Post's plan to end door-to-door mail delivery

Meanwhile, Canada Post continues to convert the remaining four million addresses that still enjoy doorstep delivery to community mailboxes, with some 621,000 homes poised to see the end of door-to-door service before 2028.
The federal budget earlier this month allocated $1.2 billion over seven years to the process, which aims to create savings of about $2.2 billion over a decade.

CEO Doug Ettinger said last month that the beleaguered organization has begun to show "early signs" of financial recovery as it wins back some of the parcel delivery market that had slipped away since 2019.
